cards.name: IVectorEffectsDataSource
cards.summary: Data-source interface behind the Pointillizer docker (Effects > Pointillizer): its properties are the docker's settings (density in tiles per square inch, screen angle, tile scale, rendering method, merge-adjacent count, tile shape, colour limit, weld overlapping tiles, keep source) and OnApply turns the selected bitmap or vector objects into a vector mosaic of many small filled shapes. It is UI state, not a document object.
use_for: vector dot / tile mosaic poster from a photo that stays sharp at any print size
pop-art halftone-dot or square-pixel portrait built from real vector shapes
mosaic logo treatment using a custom tile shape picked from the drawing
vinyl-cut or laser-ready mosaic artwork (every tile is a separate vector object)
avoid: a raster-only mosaic or pixel look: the bitmap effects Effects/Creative/Mosaic or Effects/Distort/Pixelate are far lighter
large areas at high Density: thousands of tiles make the file and redraw slow; lower DpiValue, raise CombineFactor (Merge adjacent) or limit colours
unattended COM batches: it is a docker data source, so driving it from a script is fragile; prefer opening the docker and applying by hand
cards.how: Implemented by the Pointillizer docker (cdr_effect item Pointillizer, Effects/Pointillizer, which opens docker 899d052c-fc8b-93b0-43c7-bda85ca8f417). The install's DrawUI.xml binds the docker's controls to this interface under the data-source name VectorEffectsDS, and Languages/EN/Data/strings.xml gives their English labels: Density (DpiValue, 'number of tiles per square inch'), Scale (Scale, size of each tile), Screen angle (Angle), Keep original source (KeepSource), Limit colors (LimitColors) with Number (NumColors), Method (ScaleMode from ScaleModeList, 'rendering style'), Merge adjacent (CombineFactor, 'maximum number of adjacent tiles of similar color to combine into a single tile'), Weld adjacent overlap (WeldPixels, 'weld together overlapping tiles'), Shape (Shape from ShapeList) with a Select button (OnPickShape, 'select a closed curve to use as a tile shape') and a preview (ShapePreview), and the apply button (OnApply). OnCancel and the OperationProgress bar sit in a separate Pointillizer progress dialog, shown while InProgress. No VGCore property returns it. A script can only reach it through the UI data context: app.FrameWork.Application.DataContext.GetDataSource("VectorEffectsDS") returns an ICUIDataSourceProxy whose GetProperty / SetProperty / InvokeMethod take these member names as strings (route unverified at run time).

key_members.name: DpiValue
key_members.use: long: Density, the number of tiles per square inch (the docker's Density slider)

key_members.name: Angle
key_members.use: double: Screen angle of the tile grid (the docker's spinner)

key_members.name: Scale
key_members.use: double: Scale, enlarges or shrinks each tile (the docker's Scale slider)

key_members.name: CombineFactor
key_members.use: long: Merge adjacent, the maximum number of adjacent tiles of similar colour combined into one tile

key_members.name: ScaleMode
key_members.use: string: Method, the rendering style; must be one of the entries in ScaleModeList

key_members.name: ScaleModeList
key_members.use: read-only string: the list of allowed Method (ScaleMode) entries

key_members.name: Shape
key_members.use: string: the tile shape, chosen from ShapeList

key_members.name: ShapeList
key_members.use: read-only string: available tile shapes for the Shape combo

key_members.name: ShapePreview
key_members.use: read-only variant: preview of the current tile shape shown in the docker

key_members.name: OnPickShape
key_members.use: method: Select, pick a closed curve from the drawing to use as the tile shape (only when PickShapeEnabled)

key_members.name: PickShapeEnabled
key_members.use: read-only bool: whether a custom tile shape can be picked now

key_members.name: LimitColors
key_members.use: bool: reduce the mosaic to NumColors colours

key_members.name: NumColors
key_members.use: long: colour count used when LimitColors is on (the docker enables its slider only while LimitColors is true)

key_members.name: WeldPixels
key_members.use: bool: Weld adjacent overlap, weld overlapping tiles together (settable only while WeldPixelsEnabled)

key_members.name: WeldPixelsEnabled
key_members.use: read-only bool: whether WeldPixels applies to the current settings

key_members.name: KeepSource
key_members.use: bool: Keep original source; the mosaic is placed on top of the original graphic

key_members.name: ApplyEnabled
key_members.use: read-only bool: true when the current selection can be converted; check it before OnApply

key_members.name: OnApply
key_members.use: method: run the Pointillizer on the current selection (the docker's default button)

key_members.name: OnCancel
key_members.use: method: cancel a running apply (the Cancel button of the Pointillizer progress dialog)

key_members.name: InProgress
key_members.use: read-only bool: an apply is running (shows the progress dialog's status text)

key_members.name: OperationProgress
key_members.use: double: progress of the running apply, drives the progress bar in the Pointillizer progress dialog

gotchas: Not a document object: nothing in VGCore returns it, and the type library only gives the interface; an instance lives inside the UI framework under the DrawUI.xml name VectorEffectsDS.
GetDataSource may return nothing until the Pointillizer docker has been opened at least once in the session (unverified).

ScaleMode and Shape are strings that must match an entry of ScaleModeList / ShapeList; those entries are UI text and may be localised, so read the list instead of hard-coding English names (unverified).
OnApply works on the current selection and may run in the background: poll InProgress until it is false before touching the result (unverified).

The result is one vector object per tile unless CombineFactor merges similar-colour neighbours or WeldPixels welds overlapping tiles; a high Density on a big photo can produce tens of thousands of objects.
Values set through the proxy change the docker's stored settings, so the next manual use starts from them (unverified).
cards.example:
# app = win32com.client.Dispatch("CorelDRAW.Application.25")
ds = app.FrameWork.Application.DataContext.GetDataSource("VectorEffectsDS")
ds.SetProperty("LimitColors", True)
ds.SetProperty("NumColors", 8)
ds.SetProperty("WeldPixels", True)
if ds.GetProperty("ApplyEnabled"):
    ds.InvokeMethod("OnApply")

review.changes: Corrected member meanings from the install's UI labels (Languages/EN/Data/strings.xml): DpiValue is Density in tiles per square inch, not sampling resolution; CombineFactor is Merge adjacent (similar-colour tiles combined), not density; WeldPixels welds overlapping tiles, not same-colour neighbours; ScaleMode is the Method / rendering style. OnCancel and the progress bar are in a separate progress dialog, not the docker. Updated summary, how, the avoid entry and the gotcha to match.

cards.name: _IGlobalMacroStorage
cards.summary: Hidden, member-less default interface of the GlobalMacroStorage class, the object behind the ThisMacroStorage module of a CorelDRAW global macro (GMS) VBA project. It carries nothing itself; its value is that GlobalMacroStorage sources the application events (Start, DocumentOpen, DocumentBeforeSave, Quit ...) so a GMS can react to them.
use_for: auto-run a studio setup macro when CorelDRAW starts (GlobalMacroStorage_Start)
force document settings (units, colour context) whenever a file is opened or created
a preflight hook before saving, printing or exporting print files (DocumentBeforeSave / DocumentBeforeExport)
avoid: out-of-process Python / COM scripts: this interface exposes no members; subscribe to application events with Application.AdviseEvents instead
heavy work in high-frequency events such as SelectionChange: it slows every click
cards.how: Type-library interface only (flags hidden, dual, dispatchable; no members). The coclass GlobalMacroStorage (class:GlobalMacroStorage) implements it as its default interface and declares DIVGApplicationEvents as its event source. In the VBA editor every GMS project has a ThisMacroStorage object of that class; pick GlobalMacroStorage in the module's object list and write handlers named GlobalMacroStorage_<event>, e.g. GlobalMacroStorage_DocumentOpen(ByVal Doc As Document, ByVal FileName As String).

key_members.name: GlobalMacroStorage
key_members.use: not a member (this interface has none): the coclass that implements it, i.e. ThisMacroStorage in a GMS project

key_members.name: DIVGApplicationEvents
key_members.use: not a member: the event interface GlobalMacroStorage sources; its events (Start, Quit, DocumentOpen, DocumentNew, DocumentBeforeSave, DocumentAfterSave, DocumentBeforeExport, SelectionChange, WindowActivate ...) become GlobalMacroStorage_<event> handlers

gotchas: The harvested interface has no members at all and is flagged hidden, so the Object Browser does not show it unless hidden members are shown.
Handlers only run from a GMS project that CorelDRAW loaded at start-up (the GMS folder); editing them needs VBA installed (unverified).
Application.EventsEnabled = False switches the events off for every GMS; a batch script that sets it and crashes leaves them off until restored.
Query* events (QueryDocumentSave, QueryQuit ...) can cancel the action; a bug there can block saving or quitting (unverified).
cards.example:
' VBA, in a GMS project's ThisMacroStorage module
Private Sub GlobalMacroStorage_DocumentOpen(ByVal Doc As Document, ByVal FileName As String)
    Doc.Unit = cdrMillimeter
End Sub

cards.name: ActiveView
cards.summary: The zoom and scroll state of one document window: zoom level, view centre, fit-to-page / selection / all-objects commands, multipage view and on-screen overprint or proof-colour simulation. It only changes what is shown on screen, never the document.
use_for: frame the selection or the page before an automated screenshot or review capture
set an exact zoom for a screen-recorded tutorial or client walkthrough
turn on overprint simulation or proof colours for an on-screen print check
navigate a multipage view to a given page
avoid: exporting a preview image: the view does not affect exports; use Document.ExportBitmap
measuring or positioning objects: read and set Shape position and size, not view coordinates
cards.how: Coclass whose members are on IVGActiveView. Reached as app.ActiveWindow.ActiveView (Window.ActiveView); each document window has its own. Positions are in document coordinates at the document's current Unit; Zoom is the view zoom level.

key_members.name: Zoom
key_members.use: get / set the zoom level of the window

key_members.name: OriginX
key_members.use: get / set the horizontal view origin (document coordinates)

key_members.name: OriginY
key_members.use: get / set the vertical view origin

key_members.name: SetViewPoint
key_members.use: centre the view on x, y and optionally set Zoom in one call

key_members.name: ToFitAllObjects
key_members.use: zoom to everything in the document

key_members.name: ToFitArea
key_members.use: zoom to a rectangle given as Left, Top, Right, Bottom

key_members.name: GetViewArea
key_members.use: read the visible document rectangle (x, y, width, height via ByRef arguments)

key_members.name: ShowProofColors
key_members.use: show colour proofing in this window

key_members.name: ProofColorSettings
key_members.use: the proofing profile / intent used when ShowProofColors is on

key_members.name: UseMultipageView
key_members.use: switch the window to Multipage view

key_members.name: FindPageAtPoint
key_members.use: page under a point in Multipage view

key_members.name: GetPageOrigin
key_members.use: origin of a page inside the Multipage view

gotchas: It belongs to a window: with no open document window there is no ActiveView, and app.ActiveWindow is None.
GetViewArea / GetPageOrigin return values through ByRef arguments; in Python win32com they come back as a tuple only with makepy / gencache type info (unverified).
Coordinates follow the document's Unit and origin; a script that changes Document.Unit sees different OriginX / OriginY numbers for the same view.
In Multipage view pages are laid side by side, so a page is no longer at the document origin; use GetPageOrigin or FindPageAtPoint.
View changes are cosmetic and not undoable; they also do nothing visible while Application.Optimization is on (unverified).
cards.example:
# app = win32com.client.Dispatch("CorelDRAW.Application.25")
view = app.ActiveWindow.ActiveView
view.ToFitSelection()
view.Zoom = 200
view.SimulateOverprints = True
print(view.OriginX, view.OriginY, view.Zoom)

cards.name: Application
cards.summary: The root of CorelDRAW's object model: the running app with its open documents, the active document / page / layer / selection, document creation and opening, colour factories (CreateRGBColor, CreateCMYKColor, spot colours), units, version, UI framework and app-wide settings. Every script starts here.
use_for: batch-open client .cdr / .ai / .pdf files and export them for print or web
create a new document and build a layout (flyer, label sheet, certificate run) by script
make exact brand colours (CMYK, spot) to apply to fills and outlines
speed up big generated layouts with Optimization / EventsEnabled
check the installed version before using newer calls
avoid: Quit on an instance a designer is working in: it closes everything; check Documents first
hiding the app (Visible = False) while a modal dialog may appear: the COM call then waits forever
cards.how: Coclass (flags appobject, cancreate); members are on IVGApplication, and it also implements ICUIApplication (UI framework) and sources DIVGApplicationEvents. From Python: win32com.client.Dispatch("CorelDRAW.Application.25") attaches to the running 2024 instance or starts one; in VBA / GMS macros it is the global Application, and because it is the appobject its members work unqualified (ActiveDocument, ActiveLayer ...).

key_members.name: ActiveDocument
key_members.use: the current document (None when nothing is open)

key_members.name: OpenDocument
key_members.use: open a file by path, returns the Document

key_members.name: OpenDocumentEx
key_members.use: open with a StructOpenOptions object (colour conversion, code page ...)

key_members.name: CreateDocumentEx
key_members.use: new document from a StructCreateOptions object (size, units, colour context)

key_members.name: CreateStructCreateOptions
key_members.use: make the options object for CreateDocumentEx

key_members.name: ActiveLayer
key_members.use: current layer, where Create* methods draw

key_members.name: CreateSpotColorByName
key_members.use: spot colour from a palette by colour name

key_members.name: CreateCurve
key_members.use: free Curve object for building path geometry

key_members.name: Unit
key_members.use: default unit when there is no document context

key_members.name: ConvertUnits
key_members.use: convert a value between cdrUnit units

key_members.name: Optimization
key_members.use: suspend screen updates during heavy scripts

key_members.name: Visible
key_members.use: show or hide the application window

key_members.name: FrameWork
key_members.use: UI framework: docker / dialog control, command invocation, data contexts

gotchas: Set Optimization = True (and EventsEnabled = False) only inside try / finally: if the script dies with them on, the screen stops redrawing and GMS events stay off until restored.
Measurements in method calls use the active document's Unit, which scripts should set explicitly (Document.Unit) before creating shapes; Application.Unit applies only without a document.
Dispatch("CorelDRAW.Application.25") pins the 2024 install; a bare "CorelDRAW.Application" may bind whichever version registered last (unverified).
ActiveDocument, ActiveLayer, ActiveSelectionRange are None when no document is open; check Documents.Count first.
Modal dialogs (missing fonts, import options, profile mismatch warnings) block the COM call until a person answers; set the ColorManager policies and use OpenDocumentEx options for unattended runs.
Units: CorelDRAW's object model defaults to inches unless the script sets Document.Unit (unverified for documents created from templates).
cards.example:
import win32com.client
app = win32com.client.Dispatch("CorelDRAW.Application.25")
doc = app.CreateDocument()
app.Optimization = True
red = app.CreateCMYKColor(0, 100, 100, 0)
app.ActiveLayer.CreateRectangle(1, 3, 3, 1).Fill.ApplyUniformFill(red)
app.Optimization = False
print(app.VersionMajor, app.Documents.Count)

cards.name: AppStatus
cards.summary: The status-bar progress meter: show a progress bar with a message during a long macro, advance it, change its text and let the user stop the job with Esc (Aborted).
use_for: progress feedback during a long batch export or auto-layout run inside CorelDRAW
an Esc-to-cancel loop for a long generative pattern / mosaic macro
avoid: a real dialog with buttons: this only drives the status-bar meter
unattended background runs nobody watches: it adds nothing there
cards.how: Coclass whose members are on IVGAppStatus. Reached as app.Status (Application.Status). BeginProgress(Message, CanAbort) shows the meter, UpdateProgress(Step) moves it on, Progress sets an absolute position, SetProgressMessage changes the text, EndProgress hides it.

key_members.name: BeginProgress
key_members.use: show the meter with a message; CanAbort = True lets Esc set Aborted

key_members.name: Progress
key_members.use: get / set the meter position directly

key_members.name: SetProgressMessage
key_members.use: change the text next to the meter

key_members.name: Aborted
key_members.use: read-only: True after the user pressed Esc

gotchas: Always pair BeginProgress with EndProgress (try / finally); a crashed script can leave the meter showing (unverified).
Aborted only reports Esc if BeginProgress was called with CanAbort = True, and only while CorelDRAW gets to process messages, so check it inside the loop.
The scale of Progress (percent or steps) is not in the harvest; test before relying on it (unverified).
cards.example:
# app = win32com.client.Dispatch("CorelDRAW.Application.25")
st = app.Status
st.BeginProgress("Exporting pages...", True)
for i in range(100):
    if st.Aborted:
        break
    st.Progress = i
st.EndProgress()

cards.name: AppWindow
cards.summary: The main CorelDRAW window itself: position, size, state (normal, minimized, maximized), caption, client-area size, activation and the native window handle.
use_for: restore or maximize CorelDRAW before screenshots or UI automation
get the window handle to send targeted window messages instead of global keystrokes
put the window at a fixed size so screen captures are repeatable
avoid: document windows and zoom: use Window / ActiveView
hiding the whole app: use Application.Visible
cards.how: Coclass whose members are on IVGAppWindow. Reached as app.AppWindow. WindowState takes cdrWindowState constants (cdrWindowNormal, cdrWindowMinimized, cdrWindowMaximized, cdrWindowRestore); Handle is the HWND as a long.

key_members.name: WindowState
key_members.use: get / set normal, minimized or maximized

key_members.name: Activate
key_members.use: bring the CorelDRAW window to the front

key_members.name: Left
key_members.use: window left position in screen pixels

key_members.name: ClientWidth
key_members.use: read-only width of the client area

key_members.name: ClientHeight
key_members.use: read-only height of the client area

gotchas: A minimized CorelDRAW makes screenshot- and UI-driven steps fail or return blank frames; set WindowState back to normal or maximized first.
Activate may only flash the taskbar button because of Windows focus-stealing rules (unverified).
CorelDRAW rewrites Caption when the active document changes, so a custom caption does not stick (unverified).
Win32 constants via win32com.client.constants need gencache.EnsureDispatch; with plain Dispatch use the numeric values.
cards.example:
# app = win32com.client.Dispatch("CorelDRAW.Application.25")
from win32com.client import constants as c   # after gencache.EnsureDispatch
w = app.AppWindow
w.WindowState = c.cdrWindowMaximized
w.Activate()
print(w.Handle, w.ClientWidth, w.ClientHeight)

cards.name: ArrowHead
cards.summary: One arrowhead definition: the curve of the head and how it attaches to a line (centre, line offset, outline scale), plus its name. It describes the head's shape, not its size on a particular line; that lives in ArrowHeadOptions.
use_for: arrows on callout and leader lines in infographics or technical drawings
consistent pointer style across a diagram set
registering a custom brand arrowhead made from a curve
avoid: sizing, flipping or rotating the head on one line: use Outline.StartArrowOptions / EndArrowOptions (ArrowHeadOptions)
a big decorative arrow as artwork: draw it as a curve or a Perfect Shape instead
cards.how: Coclass whose members are on IVGArrowHead. Get one from app.ArrowHeads.Item(i) (the global list), from a shape's Outline.StartArrow / EndArrow, or make one with Document.CreateArrowHead(curve) or CreateArrowHead2(curve, name); assign it back to Outline.StartArrow / EndArrow.

key_members.name: Index
key_members.use: read-only position in the global arrowhead list

key_members.name: DisplayName
key_members.use: read-only name shown in the UI (generated when no custom name)

key_members.name: Curve
key_members.use: read-only: the curve that draws the head

key_members.name: CenterX
key_members.use: read-only relative horizontal centre of the head

key_members.name: LineOffset
key_members.use: read-only relative amount the line is shortened so the head fits

key_members.name: BaseOutlineScale
key_members.use: read-only outline width relative to the head curve

key_members.name: BindToDocument
key_members.use: copy that reports coordinates in a given document's units

key_members.name: CompareWith
key_members.use: True if two arrowheads are the same

gotchas: Index numbers depend on the installed arrowhead list; find a head by DisplayName or Name instead of hard-coding an index.
CenterX, CenterY, LineOffset and BaseOutlineScale are relative, read-only values; the head drawn on a line scales with the outline width.
Curve coordinates are abstract until BindToDocument returns a copy tied to a document.
An outline with no arrowhead returns an empty / Nothing StartArrow or EndArrow (unverified).
cards.example:
# app = win32com.client.Dispatch("CorelDRAW.Application.25")
line = app.ActiveShape
heads = app.ArrowHeads
head = heads.Item(2)
print(head.Index, head.DisplayName)
line.Outline.EndArrow = head

cards.name: ArrowHeadOptions
cards.summary: Per-line arrowhead settings for one end of an outline: head length and width, offset from the line end, horizontal / vertical flip and rotation (the Arrowhead attributes of the Outline Pen).
use_for: shrink or enlarge arrowheads on thin callout lines
flip or rotate a head so it points back along the line
copy one leader line's arrow sizing to all others
avoid: choosing which head is drawn: that is the ArrowHead set on Outline.StartArrow / EndArrow
cards.how: Coclass whose members are on IVGArrowHeadOptions. Read from a shape's Outline.StartArrowOptions / EndArrowOptions, or build one with Document.CreateArrowHeadOptions(Length, Width, OffsetX, OffsetY, RotationAngle, FlipHorizontal, FlipVertical), then assign it back to the outline.

key_members.name: OffsetX
key_members.use: horizontal offset from the line end, in percent of the length

key_members.name: OffsetY
key_members.use: vertical offset, in percent of the width

key_members.name: RotationAngle
key_members.use: rotation of the head around its origin

key_members.name: Flip
key_members.use: flip by cdrFlipAxes in one call

key_members.name: CopyAssign
key_members.use: copy all values from another options object

key_members.name: FlipVerical
key_members.use: misspelt duplicate of FlipVertical kept in the type library

OffsetX / OffsetY are percentages of the head's length / width, not document units.
Options read from an outline may be a copy: change them and assign back to Outline.EndArrowOptions so the change sticks (unverified).

# app = win32com.client.Dispatch("CorelDRAW.Application.25")
ol = app.ActiveShape.Outline
opt = ol.EndArrowOptions
opt.Length = 0.2
opt.Width = 0.15
opt.FlipHorizontal = True
ol.EndArrowOptions = opt

cards.name: ArrowHeads
cards.summary: The application-wide list of arrowheads (what the arrowhead picker shows): count, 1-based access, enumeration, and adding, replacing or removing custom heads.
use_for: find an arrowhead by name for scripted diagrams
install a custom brand arrowhead for everyone using the workstation
list available heads to build an arrow style guide
avoid: arrows on one line: set the shape's Outline.StartArrow / EndArrow

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: enumerator for For Each / Python iteration

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: add a custom arrowhead to the global list; returns the stored copy

heads = app.ArrowHeads
for i in range(1, heads.Count + 1):

    print(i, h.DisplayName)

cards.name: BBoxSnapPoint
cards.summary: Extra information for a snap point that sits on an object's bounding box: which of the nine reference positions (corners, edge midpoints, centre) it is.
use_for: attach flowchart connectors to the top or bottom middle of boxes
snap or align objects by a chosen corner or centre in scripted layouts
avoid: snapping to nodes on a curve: use the generic SnapPoint returned by SnapPoints
cards.how: Coclass whose members are on IVGBBoxSnapPoint. A SnapPoint on a bounding box exposes it as SnapPoint.BBox; shape.SnapPoints.BBox(cdrReferencePoint) finds that SnapPoint directly.

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: read-only cdrReferencePoint: which corner, edge midpoint or centre this point is

Snap points of rotated objects may follow the rotated box (unverified).

# app = win32com.client.Dispatch("CorelDRAW.Application.25")
from win32com.client import constants as c   # after gencache.EnsureDispatch
a = app.ActiveSelectionRange.Item(1)
b = app.ActiveSelectionRange.Item(2)
sp = a.SnapPoints.BBox(c.cdrBottomMiddle)
print(sp.BBox.Type)
app.ActiveLayer.CreateConnector(sp, b.SnapPoints.BBox(c.cdrTopMiddle))

cards.name: CorelScriptTools

use_for: porting old Corel SCRIPT macros that call these helpers
a quick folder or file picker inside a VBA macro run by a designer
avoid: new scripts: use Application.ConvertUnits and the scripting language's own file and date functions
unattended runs: GetFileBox, GetFolder, GetColor and GetFont open modal dialogs

use_for: place markers or labels where lines cross (maps, diagrams)

cards.name: Curve
cards.summary: The path geometry of a curve object, or a free path not yet on the page: subpaths, nodes and segments, open / closed state, length and area, plus geometry tools (add rectangles, circles, ellipses and arcs, build from node arrays, contour offset, weld, hit tests, node reduction, transforms).
use_for: generate logos, badges and patterns from exact geometry
measure cut length or area for vinyl, laser or print quotes
make offset outlines (cut lines, bleeds) with Contour
clean up traced artwork by reducing nodes
avoid: simple rectangles / ellipses that should stay editable: use Layer.CreateRectangle / CreateEllipse
Boolean operations between shapes in the document: Shape.Weld / Trim / Intersect are simpler
cards.how: Coclass whose members are on IVGCurve. Reached as shape.Curve on curve shapes (convert others with Shape.ConvertToCurves first), or created free with app.CreateCurve(doc), doc.CreateCurve() or doc.CreateCurveFromArray(...), then placed with Layer.CreateCurve(curve).

key_members.name: SubPaths
key_members.use: the subpaths (separate outlines) in the curve

key_members.name: Area
key_members.use: read-only area of a closed curve

key_members.name: CreateSubPath
key_members.use: start a new subpath at x, y

key_members.name: AppendSubpathFitToPoints
key_members.use: add a smooth subpath fitted to points

key_members.name: GetCurveInfo
key_members.use: read all nodes as a CurveElement array

key_members.name: PutCurveInfo
key_members.use: replace the geometry from a CurveElement array

key_members.name: Contour
key_members.use: offset copy of the curve (inside / outside)

key_members.name: CopyAssign
key_members.use: replace this geometry with another curve's

gotchas: shape.Curve is None for rectangles, ellipses, polygons and text until the shape is converted to curves.
shape.Curve is live: each edit redraws the shape; for many edits change a GetCopy() and CopyAssign it back.
A free curve made without a document has no document units until BindToDocument.
GetCurveInfo / PutCurveInfo pass arrays of the CurveElement record, which do not marshal well through Python win32com (unverified); in Python build geometry with the AppendSubpath* methods.
Area is only meaningful for closed curves; Length counts every subpath.

crv.AppendSubpathRectangle(1, 3, 4, 1)
crv.AppendSubpathCircle(2.5, 2, 0.5)
shape = app.ActiveLayer.CreateCurve(crv)

cards.name: CurveElement
cards.summary: One record of the low-level node array that describes a curve: a point position, what the point is (subpath start, end of a line, end of a curve, or a Bezier control point), its node type and flag bits. Used to read or write whole paths in one call.
use_for: export exact path geometry (cut files, plotter output, custom formats)
rebuild or batch-modify paths fast in VBA (one PutCurveInfo instead of many node edits)
copy geometry between documents without the clipboard
avoid: Python win32com scripts: record arrays marshal poorly; use Curve.AppendSubpath* or node objects
single node edits: use Node objects
cards.how: A record (struct) type, not an object: it is never created on its own. Curve.GetCurveInfo and SubPath.GetCurveInfo return an array of it; Curve.PutCurveInfo, Curve.CreateSubPathFromArray and Document.CreateCurveFromArray take one. ElementType uses cdrCurveElementType (cdrElementStart, cdrElementLine, cdrElementCurve, cdrElementControl), NodeType uses cdrNodeType (cdrCuspNode, cdrSmoothNode, cdrSymmetricalNode) and Flags holds cdrCurveElementFlags bits (cdrFlagSelected, cdrFlagUser, cdrFlagClosed, cdrFlagValid).

key_members.name: PositionX
key_members.use: x of the point, in document units

key_members.name: ElementType
key_members.use: what the point is (cdrCurveElementType): start, line end, curve end or control point

key_members.name: Flags
key_members.use: byte of cdrCurveElementFlags bits (selected, user, closed, valid)

gotchas: A Bezier segment is stored as two cdrElementControl records followed by the cdrElementCurve end point; a straight segment is one cdrElementLine record (order unverified).
Each subpath starts with a cdrElementStart record; the closed state is carried in Flags (cdrFlagClosed) (unverified).
Arrays of this record (SAFEARRAY of a user-defined type) do not marshal reliably through Python win32com late binding (unverified); use VBA or the Curve AppendSubpath* methods.
Positions use the document's current Unit when the curve is bound to a document.
cards.example:
' VBA
Dim info() As CurveElement, i As Long
info = ActiveShape.Curve.GetCurveInfo
For i = LBound(info) To UBound(info)
    Debug.Print info(i).ElementType, info(i).PositionX, info(i).PositionY
Next i
ActiveShape.Curve.PutCurveInfo info
